definitions.explanation: The time by which a person must be home or the time at which the gate or entrance of a dormitory, school, or similar facility is locked. Commonly used for household curfews set by parents.

examples.japanese: {門限|もんげん}に{遅|おく}れて{怒|おこ}られた。
examples.english: I got scolded for missing my curfew.

examples.japanese: {大学|だいがく}の{寮|りょう}には{門限|もんげん}があって、{夜|よる}11{時|じ}までに{戻|もど}らないといけない。
examples.english: The university dorm has a curfew, and you have to be back by 11 p.m.

notes:
{門限|もんげん} literally means "gate limit" ({門|もん} = gate + {限|げん} = limit). It originally referred to the time when the gate of a compound was locked, but now commonly means any curfew.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {門限|もんげん}がある (to have a curfew)
- {門限|もんげん}に{間|ま}に{合|あ}う (to make it home by curfew)
- {門限|もんげん}に{遅|おく}れる (to miss curfew)
- {門限|もんげん}を{破|やぶ}る (to break curfew)
- {門限|もんげん}を{過|す}ぎる (to be past curfew)

USAGE:
Most commonly used when talking about household rules set by parents for teenagers, or the closing time of dormitories and student housing. The word also applies to traditional Japanese inns ({旅館|りょかん}) and some hostels that lock their doors at a set time.
